verdict.justification: Both deliverables accurately aggregate the Tour Manager and Production Company schedules into a clean P&L report with proper category mapping. However, Deliverable B is superior because it preserves exact source precision, whereas Deliverable A wraps its withholding tax formulas in `ROUND(..., 2)`. Because Germany's withholding tax rate is 15.825%, rounding Munich ($99,117 * 15.825% = $15,685.26525) and Berlin ($132,812 * 15.825% = $21,017.499) at the stop level causes Deliverable A's total withholding tax ($191,321.57) and Net Revenue ($852,428.43) to be off by a cent from the reference file's exact calculation ($191,321.56425). Additionally, Deliverable B provides a much more comprehensive workbook architecture, including dedicated `Revenue Detail` (with a regional summary tie-out), `Expense Detail`, and `Source Reconciliation` tabs, as well as a `% of Gross Revenue` column on the P&L. Deliverable B also keeps distinct line items separate (`Transfer Cars` vs. `Car Service`), whereas Deliverable A merges them onto a single row (`Transfer Cars / Car Service`).

decisive_issues.issue: Prematurely rounds stop-level withholding taxes to two decimal places, causing a $0.01 rounding discrepancy in Germany's withholding tax and Total Net Revenue compared to the reference file.
